Drop connections when the network changes
Switching between Wi-Fi and mobile data kills the connections that went through the old one. Dropping them right away lets apps reconnect instead of waiting out a timeout.
Access control — which apps go through the tunnel
All apps go through the tunnel — the checkboxes below change nothing until you pick another mode.
Manage what the app can notify you about
The ongoing notification itself can\'t be turned off — Android requires it while the VPN is running.
A transient notification while a subscription update is running
The only way to notice a subscription that silently stopped updating
The short \"Profile Updater\" notification can\'t be turned off here — Android requires it while the update runs in the background. It stays hidden for updates that finish quickly.
Remind before the subscription runs out, once it has, and when traffic use crosses a threshold — all set by the panel
Requires the panel to send expiry/traffic reminder headers; if it never sends any, no reminders are shown, regardless of this switch.
Sound and vibration for this notification
The app needs the notification permission to show the tunnel status and warnings when the subscription is about to expire or run out of traffic.

The power button here only shows the background with the profile off and on; it connects nothing.
Changes while the VPN is off. The congestion controller paces TCP inside mipstack; CUBIC is the default.
Choosing another node in a group closes the connections going through that group, so apps reconnect through the new node at once. Off, they stay on the old node until they end.

Opens the core\'s controller on 127.0.0.1:9090 for the Zashboard dashboard in Settings → Active Tunnel, guarded by Zashboard\'s own secret, made once and kept. While it is on, it is the only controller: the controller settings in Override are cleared and locked, and a profile\'s own controller gives way to it.
The External Controller group in Override is cleared — the address, its TLS, CORS and Secret: while Zashboard is on, its controller is the only one.
The running VPN reloads its configuration with the controller open to Zashboard.
Debug → Zashboard holds the controller: 127.0.0.1:9090 with its own secret. These settings are off while it is on.

The dashboard\'s settings, saved backends and cache. An open dashboard closes.
Profiles, their files and per-profile settings. The VPN turns off.
Apps marked “from subscription” go around the VPN by the profile\'s own settings, in any mode. Apps ticked here in “Deny selected apps” are added to them.
The profile lets only the apps marked “from subscription” through the VPN. Apps ticked here in “Allow selected apps” are added to them; “Deny selected apps” has no effect with such a profile.
Allow Autostart for Prizrak-Box on this screen: without it the system does not let the VPN start after a reboot.
